assessment: This valuable article describes a fragility index based on the geometry of chi-square tests. The result is linked to the concept of measurement error in outcomes, such that one can directly quantify how less-than-perfect sensitivity or specificity will call into question the statistical significance of a particular finding. The methodology rests upon solid mathematical exposition and several real-world examples of both interventional and observational studies. Noteworthy extensions for future considerations would be the application of this approach to censored outcomes.
